verified_against_binary: v2.37.1 removes prose that encodes its own position on the page, and adds a check so it cannot return. A reader spotted 'The ordering below' inside the 'What is not established' box on the detection page -- a box that is last on its page, so nothing was below it. Auditing the class found three instances, and two of them were wrong BEFORE the redesign rather than broken by it: that box has always been last. The third, 'not part of the verified material above', was correct on the entry page and became wrong on the contract page when the redesign moved that callout above the rules. The underlying issue is that the site treats a fact as a self-contained unit -- the same string renders on a topic page, on the contract page, in the Markdown twin and in facts.json for other consumers -- so any wording that assumes one layout is false in the rest. All three rewritten to say what they mean without reference to layout. New validator rule scans every published prose string (rules, details, caveats, page summaries, blurbs, open questions, tool blurbs, router rows, top-5 entries) and rejects bare positional references while allowing numeric comparisons such as 'above 1,024 characters'. Verified against all three original wordings before landing; a rule that cannot fail is worth nothing. No fact, tier, severity or date changed.
note: Found by a reader on a phone, not by any automated check -- the class had survived every prior pass because each instance reads perfectly well in isolation.
